title: fix(layout): useAppShellBranding restores the favicon it replaced (objectui#10040)
body:
Fixes #10040
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`useAppShellBranding` (`packages/layout`, `AppShell.tsx`) now scopes its favicon write to the mount, the same way objectui#8637 scoped its `document.title` write:

- when `branding.favicon` is set and the page has an icon link (`#favicon`, else `link[rel="icon"]`), the effect records the link element and its `href` **attribute**, then writes the branded URL exactly as before;
- the same cleanup that restores the title puts that attribute back (`setAttribute`), or removes it when the link had none;
- no `favicon`, or no icon link: nothing is written and nothing is restored. The hook still never creates an icon link.

Why the attribute and not `link.href`: the property is the URL resolved against the document, so the console's own icon link (`href=""` in `apps/console/index.html` until an operator favicon exists) reads back as the page's URL. Restoring through the property would point the icon at the page itself. Measured in happy-dom (the environment-control test) and by ablation leg 2 below.

## Dispatch mechanism assumptions A1–A4, measured

- **A1 holds, with one correction.** The change mirrors the title restore (capture in the effect, restore in the same cleanup). The "remove a link the effect created" branch does not apply: the effect never creates a link (it writes only when one exists, and `content/docs/layout/app-shell.mdx` says so), so there is nothing to remove; ablation leg 5 pins that it stays that way. The capture has to be the attribute, not the property (above).
- **A2 holds.** Absent `branding.favicon`, the captured link stays null: no write, no restore (pin, and ablation leg 3).
- **A3: no fight; order measured.** A scratch harness (never committed, deleted after the run) mounted the real `FaviconSync` from `apps/console` as the first sibling under a `MemoryRouter` (the console mounts it as the first child of `BrowserRouter`, ahead of the routes) and the real hook under `/apps/:appName/*`, with `getFaviconUrl` mocked, logging every write to the icon link. Order within one navigation commit: shell cleanup (restore), then `FaviconSync`'s effect, then the shell's effect (capture + branded write).
  - No operator favicon. This branch: `/apps/a` shows A; `/apps/b` restores `""` then writes B; `/apps/plain` ends `""`; `/home` ends `""`. On the branch point `86982ace0`: `/apps/plain` stays **B** and `/home` stays **A**, which is the card's defect reproduced at DOM level.
  - Operator favicon O configured. Every end state is identical on this branch and on `86982ace0`: the restore puts back O, which is what `FaviconSync` writes next anyway.
  - Pre-existing and unchanged here: with an operator favicon configured, an in-app navigation (`/apps/a` to `/apps/a/page-2`) makes `FaviconSync` write O over the branded icon, on both trees. Reported to the seat as an out-of-scope finding, not addressed in this PR.
- **A4: pins written; red counts below.**

## Tests

New: `packages/layout/src/__tests__/app-shell-branding-favicon-restore.test.tsx`, beside the `app-shell-branding-title-*` pins: 9 tests (1 environment control, 8 pins).

Ablations, each a trap-armed mutation with a blob-hash restore proof. The tests import `../AppShell` source directly, so no `dist/` is on the resolution path.

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `AppShell.tsx` set to the branch point `86982ace0` | 5 failed, 4 passed |
| 2 | capture through the `link.href` property | 5 failed, 4 passed |
| 3 | cleanup writes the icon even when the effect wrote none | 1 failed (the no-`favicon` pin), 8 passed |
| 4 | forward write removed | 5 failed, 4 passed |
| 5 | effect creates an icon link when the page has none | 1 failed (the no-icon-link pin), 8 passed |

Every pin is red in at least one leg. The two that are green on the branch point (write while mounted; no `favicon` means no write) pin existing behaviour and go red in legs 4 and 3. Every restore leg ended with the file's blob equal to the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Local verification at `d10a9ad9d`

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/layout^..." build`: exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout type-check`: exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the new test file
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/layout/ apps/console/src/__tests__/tabTitleAfterNavigation.test.tsx`: 25 files, 245 tests passed
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-control-bytes`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-changeset-fixed`: all exit 0; `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the three paths: NOT GOVERNED
- eslint on the two touched TS files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 2 files, 0 errors, 1 warning (`react-refresh/only-export-components` on the `useAppShellBranding` export, present on the branch point too). Narrowing stated: the population is the root `eslint.config.js` block for `**/*.{ts,tsx}`; the resolved config has empty `parserOptions` (no type-aware linting) and no custom rule reads other files, so this diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

Pending changesets that name `AppShell.tsx` / `useAppShellBranding` (the 4830, 6871, 6872 and 8637 ones) were re-read: none is made false by this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, reported to the seat and not filed: `FaviconSync`'s route-keyed re-apply writes the operator favicon over a branded app favicon on every in-app navigation when both are configured; it is the favicon twin of the title race objectui#8637 removed.
- `content/docs/layout/app-shell.mdx` says the colour properties are removed again when the shell unmounts, and does not mention that the title and (now) the favicon are restored too. The sentence stays true; the omission is noted, not addressed here (outside the claimed surface).
- The hook sets only `href`; `link.type`, which the console's boot script and `FaviconSync` set by file extension, is left as it was. Observation only.
